key_insight: Enforcing linear completeness enables provable PIML convergence, addressing a learning-induced error term that may persist under mesh refinement when only rigid-body displacement invariance is enforced.
engineering_relevance: The approach supports efficient substructure-based finite element analysis by learning numerical shape functions while preserving conformity and recovering optimal convergence rates.
method: Learn substructure numerical shape functions from material distributions or element geometries.
Bound numerical error using finite element discretization error and network generalization error.
Reconstruct transition-matrix columns using linear displacement constraints to enforce linear completeness.
evidence_signal: The abstract reports H1- and L2-norm convergence results and numerical experiments demonstrating optimal convergence rates, good generalization, and numerical stability.
watch_item: Linear completeness addresses convergence consistency, but practical accuracy still depends on network generalization; the abstract does not quantify performance outside the tested cases.
paper_title: Convergence and error analysis of problem-independent machine learning (PIML) with linear completeness
